source_caption:
To ground the profound emotional weight of Dr. Louise Banks’s non-linear journey, director Denis Villeneuve utilized Max Richter’s devastatingly mournful track “On the Nature of Daylight” to bookend the film. During the editing process, Villeneuve used the existing string piece as a temporary placeholder for the opening and closing montages depicting the life and death of Louise’s daughter. When original composer Jóhann Jóhannsson attempted to write a bespoke track to replace it, both he and Villeneuve ultimately concluded that Richter’s composition had perfectly embedded itself into the film’s DNA. In a rare display of cinematic ego-checking, Jóhannsson agreed to step aside for those crucial sequences, allowing Richter’s existing music to underscore the script’s core emotional thesis: the courage to embrace love and loss even when knowing the inevitable, tragic outcome.

Arrival (2016), directed by Denis Villeneuve, starring Amy Adams, Jeremy Renner, Forest Whitaker, Michael Stuhlbarg. When mysterious extraterrestrial spacecraft touch down across the globe, an elite linguistics professor is recruited by the military to decode the alien language and determine their intentions, uncovering a profound revelation that alters her perception of time.

source_details.synopsis: Arrival is a 2016 American science fiction drama film directed by Denis Villeneuve and written by Eric Heisserer, based on the 1998 novella "Story of Your Life" by Ted Chiang. The film stars Amy Adams as Louise Banks, a linguist engaged by the United States Army to discover how to communicate with extraterrestrials who have arrived on Earth, before tensions lead to war. Jeremy Renner, Forest Whitaker, and Michael Stuhlbarg appear in supporting roles. Arrival had its world premiere at the Venice Film Festival on September 1, 2016, and was released theatrically in the United States by Paramount Pictures on November 11, 2016.
